methodology.value: Segmentation from polling 14 Mar-7 Apr 2025, N=13,464 (k-means after PCA, gradient boosting classifier); other waves 28 May-2 Jun 2025 N=4,156; 27-30 Jun N=2,030; Wales 19 Jun-2 Jul N=883; VI 23-30 Jun N=4,756. Weighted to GB adults. Northern Ireland excluded.

source.segmentation_inputs: Economic left-right; authoritarian-libertarian; moral foundations (Care, Loyalty, Authority, Autonomy, Equality, Purity); political/civic engagement; institutional trust; individual responsibility; conspiracy susceptibility; populism; simplicity/complexity; need for chaos; compromise; free speech; multiculturalism/nativism; authoritarian parenting styles (pp. 260-261). Demographics are NOT inputs (p262).
source.evidence_rules: Every number is either (a) read from a rendered chart image, or (b) stated in running report prose and checked against the text layer. No chart value was taken from the text layer (whose chart numbers are unordered). Unreadable/unlabelled values are null. No estimates.

Progressive Activists.summary: Young-leaning, graduate, highly secular and politically engaged left. Social-justice and global outlook (Gaza, climate, inequality); see structural forces rather than individual effort as driving outcomes; most pro-immigration segment and least proud to be British. Trust experts, judges and public broadcasters but not politicians; reluctant to compromise and open to radical institutional change. High income but low wealth: renters, flatsharers, student debt. Drifting from Labour to the Greens (and SNP/Plaid).

Traditional Conservatives.summary: Oldest, wealthiest, most White and Christian segment; rural home-owners. Strongly migration-sceptic and opposed to strict net zero, but institutionally trusting, optimistic, purposeful and risk-averse. Strongest party identity; Conservative base now narrowly leaning Reform.

Dissenting Disruptors.summary: Frustrated, anti-establishment, populist segment in post-industrial towns: mostly White, non-graduate, financially struggling, close to home, male-leaning. Lowest institutional trust, most lonely and least respected, most likely to say system is rigged and institutions should burn, want a rule-breaking strong leader and people (not politicians) to decide. Most opposed to multiculturalism, free-speech maximalist, most conspiracy-prone. Often non-voters, but Reform UK's core base.
